value.title: Number claims and delivery at merge
value.summary: Roadmap 001 step s11. `pij claim <kind>` hands out the next number per project and kind with the claiming seat on record, so parallel PMs never collide; and `pij delivered <pr>`, run by whoever merges (ruling C23), records which requirements and steps a merged PR delivered, puts it on the owning PM's card, and prints the ddocs edits for the PM's next docs PR.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Numbers (plans, PRDs, roadmaps, blueprints, migrations) are handed out by hand today: pm-001 checks folders and branches and logs claims in a markdown LOG, and harness builder only sees local worktrees. Requirement and step states lag the code because nobody records delivery at merge. This plan adds a store-backed claim verb and a merge-time delivery verb. Per ruling C23, delivery is a verb the merger runs once (no poll, no webhook), and pij never pushes: it prints the `ddocs set` edits that fill `delivered_by`, and the PM puts them in its next docs PR.

sections.name: goals
value: Two seats claiming the same kind at once always get different numbers, and every claim names its seat.
A claim is released when its work merges or its seat closes.
After a merge, one command records what the PR delivered and tells the owning PM, without any polling.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Editing the project docs from the daemon: pij prints the edits and never commits or pushes them (C23).
A GitHub webhook or any periodic check of PR state.
Changing how plans are scaffolded (harness plan new keeps its --ordinal flag; the claim supplies the number).

value.claim: Claim. `pij claim <kind> [--project <slug>] --for <subject>` returns the next number for (project, kind) and records it with the claiming seat, subject and time in the store (migration 0033). Known kinds and their widths: plan, prd, roadmap, blueprint (3 digits), migration (4 digits); any other lowercase kind is accepted with 3 digits. The next number is one more than the highest of: the numbers already claimed for that kind, and the numbers already present in the project's main checkout (docs/plans/NNN-*, docs/project/prds|roadmaps|blueprints/NNN-*, crates/store/migrations/NNNN_*), read in-process with no launch.

No collisions. Ten concurrent claims for one (project, kind) get ten distinct consecutive numbers, under one store write transaction each (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and a unique (project, kind, number) key. Claims for two projects never interact.

Release. A claim is released (kept as history with released-at and reason) when its seat is tombstoned (hooked into publish_tombstone, the one path for close, reap and revive), when `pij delivered` sees the number land on main, or by `pij claim release <kind> <number>` from the claiming seat or the prime. A released number is never handed out again. `pij claims [--project]` lists open and released claims.

Delivered (ruling C23). `pij delivered <pr> [--project <slug>]` reads the merged PR once with gh (resolved like ddocs: PIJ_GH, else PATH, absolute, once at daemon start; tests inject a fake), refuses by name if the PR is not merged, and takes the delivered addresses from the PR body's `Delivers:` line (full ddocs addresses such as `docs/project/prds/001-pij-community.dd.json#requirements/req-07` and roadmap step addresses). It records (project, PR, address, merge commit, recorded by, time) in the store, idempotently.

Edits printed, never applied. `pij delivered` prints, and returns in --json, the exact `ddocs set` commands that set `delivered_by` on each delivered requirement and the plan cell on each step, for the PM's next docs PR. It writes no project file, commits nothing and pushes nothing.

The PM's card. The delivery is posted on the owning PM's card within one event: the PM is the live holder of the project's `pm-<roadmap number>` role when s04's assignments exist, else the seat given by `--pm <seat>`; with neither, the receipt says no PM was told. Claims whose numbers appear in the PR's files are released (AC3).

Convention. The pij skill's community procedures (skills/pij/references/community/) say how to claim a number, and that every PR body carries a `Delivers:` line; the PR template gains the line. The procedures stop telling PMs to ask pm-001 for numbers.

Cost. `pij claim` and `pij claims` launch nothing (store and in-process directory reads). `pij delivered` costs one gh launch per call by absolute path, recorded by the spawn counter and covered by spawn_sites.rs. Nothing runs on a timer.

Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents both verbs and their refusals; the skill's verb coverage and shim tables carry them. In this PR: roadmap s11 goes to complete with its plan cell set to docs/plans/196-claims-delivery; req-20 and req-21 go to shipped; c-claims and c-merge-delivery go to shipped. All project docs validate clean.

value.title: Claims and delivery at merge
value.brief: AC1 to AC9. One coder. Migration 0033 (claims and deliveries); `pij claim`, `pij claims`, `pij claim release`; the tombstone hook; `pij delivered` with an injected gh; the printed edits; the PM card post; skill procedures and PR template; docs and flips. AC6's holder lookup uses s04's assignments if plan 195 has merged; otherwise `--pm` only, and AC6 is checked against that. CS-3.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code facts (2026-11-04, main 6ccd4d8): no GitHub API, webhook or merge hook anywhere; the daemon never calls gh (reqwest is a dependency but unused for PRs). No project-scoped counter exists; streams.ordinal (crates/store/src/orchestration.rs:412-439) shows the reserve-under-BEGIN-IMMEDIATE pattern with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; begin_write is crates/store/src/migrate.rs:267-268. Seat card: POST /v1/state -> seat_state (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:636, 2682); report handler at mod.rs:3563. Tombstone: publish_tombstone in crates/store/src/registry.rs:48-99 (close, reap and revive all pass through it). Schemas: pij/prd requirement rows have optional `delivered_by` (.dd/schemas/pij/prd/schema.json:143-183); roadmap steps have state, plan and delivers (.dd/schemas/pij/roadmap/schema.json:66-118). Latest migration 0031; 0032 is claimed by plan 195, 0033 by this plan.

value.question: Ruled C23: delivery is a verb the merger runs (`pij delivered <pr>`), printing the ddocs edits for the PM's docs PR; no poll, no webhook, pij never pushes.
value.answer: C23, folded into AC4 and AC5.

value.question: Should `pij claim` also scan remote branches for numbers already used there (the gap that made harness builder miss plans on other branches)? Recommended: no. Scanning needs git launches; from this plan on, claims are the authority, and the main checkout scan covers merged work.

value.risk: A PR body without a `Delivers:` line records nothing and nobody notices.
value.mitigation: `pij delivered` refuses by name when the line is missing, and the PR template carries it (AC7).

value.risk: gh missing or unauthenticated on the merger's machine.
value.mitigation: Named refusal with the install or auth step; doctor reports the gh pij will use.

value.risk: Numbers used by work in flight before claims existed collide with the first claims.
value.mitigation: The main-checkout scan plus pm-001 importing today's LOG claims (plans 190 to 196, migrations 0031 to 0033) with `pij claim` at first use.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use a private daemon, a scratch store and a fake gh; never the prod daemon or a real PR.
Builds scoped with -p; check `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` first; stop and tell pm-001 under 25 GB.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, never push refs/notes/*. No node_modules: TS proof is CI on the exact head.
One push per review round; no pushes after a PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
